mainTopic: Practical life advice and safety warnings of the חכמים: lists of instructions from רבינו הקדוש and others, dangers to avoid, and the stories of אגרת בת מחלת
overview: This amud opens mid-sentence, finishing the reason for advice about marrying a woman who was married before: 'not all fingers are equal.' It then gives two short teachings about acts that are both a מצוה and good for a person: a fair loan arrangement and marriage. Next comes a list of four commands רבינו הקדוש gave his sons: avoid the mockers of שכנציב, beware 'the bed of an ארמית' (explained three ways), do not evade taxes, and keep away from an ox coming up from the marsh. That leads to more teachings about dangerous oxen, the calls used to drive animals, אביי's list of habits that cause צרעת, and רב פפא's warnings about cats and snakes. Then come two more lists of three instructions given to רבי, by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, covering court cases, honest buying, waiting after immersion, going out alone at night, candles, and new bathhouses. The warning about going out at night leads to stories of אגרת בת מחלת meeting רבי חנינא בן דוסא and אביי, who decreed that she stay out of inhabited places. The גמרא then asks why harmful forces are still seen there, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Not all fingers are equal
steps.stepSummary: The reason for the previous instruction ends: people are not all the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because not all fingers are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. On the previous amud, the advice was not to marry a divorced woman while her first husband is alive, and איכא דאמרי ('some say') the advice applies even to an אלמנה. This line gives the reason for that wider view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two men can be as different as two fingers on one hand. A woman who remarries may compare her new husband to her first one and come to look down on him. The image teaches that comparison between spouses can ruin a marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new teaching. It is only the closing reason for advice that was given on the previous part of the דף.

phrases.english: For not all fingers are equal.
phrases.notes: Explains the previous advice: the second husband may not measure up to the first in her eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning of an instruction earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People differ, and a woman may compare her new husband to her first one, so (according to איכא דאמרי) even marrying an אלמנה invites trouble.

steps.title: A מצוה and a big benefit: eating fruits through a fair loan arrangement
steps.stepSummary: Lending money and eating the fruits of a field held as security, with a proper deduction, is both a מצוה and good for the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה and a great benefit to the body: one who eats fruits and not payment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new piece of advice: there is a deal that is both a מצוה and a real personal gain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender holds a field as security (משכנתא) and eats its fruits, but takes their value off the loan. The borrower gets a loan, which is a מצוה. The lender gets food instead of forbidden interest (רבית). Both sides benefit and no איסור is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: a great benefit to the body, a big personal gain
fruits, here the produce of a field
payment or profit, here meaning interest

phrases.english: A מצוה and a great bodily benefit:
phrases.notes: A set phrase for something that helps both your soul and your body.

phrases.english: one who eats fruits and not payment.
phrases.notes: רשב"ם explains: he holds a field as security and eats its fruits, but they come off the loan, so it isn't interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of instructions with a new item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a field's fruits through a fair, deducted loan arrangement is both a מצוה and a personal benefit.

steps.title: A מצוה and a pure body: marrying a woman
steps.stepSummary: Marrying a woman is a מצוה and keeps a person's thoughts pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה and a pure body: one who marries a woman and has children.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a matching teaching built on the same pattern as the previous step: an act that is a מצוה and also keeps the body pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage protects a man from improper thoughts (הרהור), which is the 'pure body' part. He also fulfills the מצוה of having children. Another reading is that he should marry even if he already has children.

keyTerms.meaning: a pure body, free of improper thoughts

steps.whatToRemember: The two 'מצוה וגוף' teachings form a pair. One gives a big benefit (a fair loan arrangement); the other gives a pure body (marriage).

phrases.english: A מצוה and a pure body:
phrases.notes: Same pattern as the previous step.

phrases.english: one who marries a woman, and he has children.
phrases.notes: Some explain he will merit children; רשב"ם says he marries even though he already has children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second half of the 'מצוה וגוף' pair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marriage is both a מצוה and a safeguard of purity.

steps.title: רבי's four commands: do not live among mockers
steps.stepSummary: רבינו הקדוש gave his sons four commands. The first: do not live in שכנציב, because its people are mockers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our holy רבי commanded his sons four things: Do not live in שכנציב, because they are mockers, and they will draw you into their mockery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list of family instructions, this time from רבינו הקדוש (רבי יהודה הנשיא). It gives the first command right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is not only the mockers themselves but their pull on you. Living around people who make fun of everything slowly draws you into the same habit and away from serious Torah learning. Where you live shapes who you become.

keyTerms.meaning: Our holy רבי, רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for choosing your surroundings carefully, because environment affects behavior.

phrases.english: Four things commanded
our holy Rabbi to his sons:
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה.

phrases.english: Do not live in Shekhantziv,
because they are mockers,
and they will draw you into mockery.
phrases.notes: They will pull you away from serious Torah learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ אֶת בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new list of instructions from a different sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not live in a place full of mockers, because they will pull you into their ways.

steps.title: Second command: do not sit on an Aramean woman's bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי's second command is a short, puzzling phrase that the גמרא will explain next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The second command is quoted in a cryptic form. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא gives three explanations of what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is unclear: it could be a hint or a literal warning. The גמרא offers three readings. Two treat it as a hint (sleeping without קריאת שמע, marrying a גיורת), and one takes it literally (an actual ארמית, because of רב פפא).
steps.confusionAlert: The next three steps give three different explanations. Two read the phrase as a hint, and the third (step 8) takes it literally.

phrases.english: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in רבי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cryptic warning about 'the bed of an ארמית,' explained in the next steps.

steps.title: First explanation: do not go to sleep without קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: Some say the 'Aramean bed' means going to sleep without saying קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: that you should not go to sleep without reciting שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first explanation of the cryptic command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going to bed without קריאת שמע על המטה is like sleeping the way a gentile does, with no connection to ה׳. Your bed becomes an 'Aramean bed.' On this reading, the command is about holiness in daily habits.

keyTerms.meaning: some say, there are those who say

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: This is the first of three explanations.

phrases.english: that you should not go to sleep without reciting Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: דְּלָא תִּיגְנֵי בְּלָא קְרִיַּת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the cryptic phrase from step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implied question: what does 'the bed of an ארמית' mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bed without קריאת שמע is a 'gentile bed.'

steps.title: Second explanation: do not marry a convert
steps.stepSummary: Others say the 'Aramean bed' means marrying a גיורת, a woman who was once an Aramean.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: that you should not marry a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different explanation of the same command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'the bed of an ארמית' is read as the marriage bed of a woman who came from an Aramean background, meaning a גיורת. This is family advice about marriage for רבי's sons, not a statement that a גיורת is forbidden. The next step adds a third explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: This is personal advice, not a halachic prohibition. Marrying a גיורת is fully permitted to a Jew who is not a כהן.

phrases.english: And some say:
that you should not marry a convert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative interpretation to step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Same implied question: what does 'the bed of an ארמית' mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to marrying a woman of Aramean origin, a גיורת.

steps.title: A third explanation: a real Aramean woman's bed
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says the 'Aramean bed' means the actual bed of a non-Jewish woman, because of what happened to רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: it means an actual Aramean woman, because of the incident with רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to understand רבי's puzzling second command. Here the words are taken literally: do not sit on the bed of a non-Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two explanations read the phrase as a hint, either to skipping קריאת שמע or to marrying a גיורת. This view reads it plainly and points to a real danger. רב פפא sat on a non-Jewish woman's bed, a dead baby was found under it, and he was falsely blamed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of the 'Aramean bed': sleeping without קריאת שמע, marrying a גיורת, and literally sitting on a non-Jewish woman's bed (because of רב פפא).
steps.confusionAlert: The story of רב פפא is not written out in this text. The גמרא only mentions it, and the full story is told by the commentators and in the Sefaria translation.

phrases.english: And some say:
an actual Aramean woman,
and because of the incident of Rav Pappa.
phrases.notes: He was falsely accused when a dead baby was found under the woman's bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third alternative explanation of the phrase, parallel to steps 6 and 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'Aramean bed' is literally a non-Jewish woman's bed, because of the danger of a false accusation.

steps.title: Third command: do not evade taxes
steps.stepSummary: רבי warns his sons not to sneak away from paying the government tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not run away from the tax, because they may catch you and take everything you have.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with רבי's third command: pay your taxes and do not try to escape them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is practical. If you are caught dodging the tax, the government may take everything you own, not just the tax amount. This is advice about protecting yourself.

phrases.english: And do not make yourself escape from the tax,
lest they find you
and take from you everything that you have.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from explaining the second command to the list of רבי's commands
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not evade taxes, because you risk losing all your property.

steps.title: Fourth command: do not stand in front of an ox coming from the marsh
steps.stepSummary: רבי warns not to stand in front of an ox as it comes up from the marshland, because it is especially dangerous then.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not stand in front of an ox when it comes up from the marsh, because the שטן dances between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's fourth and last command: stay out of the way of an ox coming up from the marsh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the שטן 'dances between its horns' is a vivid way of saying the ox is wild and dangerous at that moment. It means the ox is likely to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The Satan, a force of harm

phrases.english: And do not stand in front of the ox
at the time when it comes up from the marsh,
because the Satan dances between its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of commands
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid standing before an ox coming up from the marsh, because it is dangerous then.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's four commands: do not live in שכנציב, beware the 'Aramean bed,' do not evade taxes, and do not stand before an ox coming from the marsh.

steps.title: Which ox and when: a black ox in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל says the warning applies to a black ox during the days of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל said: this is about a black ox, and in the days of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: A Sage narrows רבי's fourth command. He tells us exactly when the danger is greatest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי spoke about oxen in general. רבי שמואל limits the warning to a black ox in the spring month of ניסן, when oxen are most aggressive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel said:
With a black ox, and in the days of Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the fourth command
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ox warning applies especially to a black ox in ניסן.

steps.title: How far to keep away from an ox
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא teaches a ברייתא: keep fifty אמות from a שור תם, and stay out of sight of a שור מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא taught: keep fifty אמות away from a שור תם, and from a שור מועד keep as far as its eyes can see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that gives exact distances for staying safe from an ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שור תם has not gored repeatedly, so fifty אמות is enough. A שור מועד has already gored three times, so you must go so far that it cannot see you at all. The more dangerous the ox, the farther you must stay away.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox with no repeated history of goring
An ox known to gore, having done so three times
As far as its eyes can see

steps.confusionAlert: Here שור תם and שור מועד are used for personal safety distances, not for the usual דין of how much damages the owner pays.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya taught:
One keeps away from an innocuous ox — fifty cubits;
from a forewarned ox — as far as its eyes can see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds measured distances to the theme of the dangerous ox
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep 50 אמות from a שור תם, and stay out of sight of a שור מועד.

steps.title: Even an ox eating is dangerous: climb up and kick away the ladder
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי מאיר: even when an ox has its head in its feeding basket, climb to the roof and throw the ladder down after you.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: even if the ox's head is in its basket, go up to the roof and throw the ladder out from under you.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching about oxen exaggerates on purpose to show how careful you must be around them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an ox busy eating is harmless. רבי מאיר says that even then you should run to the roof and remove the ladder so the ox cannot follow. This is exaggerated language meant to stress caution.

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Even if the ox's head is in the basket —
go up to the roof
and throw the ladder out from beneath you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the warning about oxen, even when they seem calm
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flee from an ox even when it appears busy and harmless.

steps.title: The calls used to drive an ox, lion, camel, and ship
steps.stepSummary: רב lists the special sounds people use to lead or drive different animals and a ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the call for an ox is 'hen hen'; for a lion, 'zeh zeh'; for a camel, 'da da'; and for a ship, 'heleni hayya hela vehilook hulya.'
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of animals, רב records the cries used to direct an ox, a lion, a camel, and the workers pulling a ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the גמרא has been talking about oxen, it adds רב's practical teaching on how each animal is driven. The ship call was the chant used by workers pulling a boat with ropes along a river.

keyTerms.meaning: Call, cry used to drive an animal

steps.whatToRemember: The ox theme moves from רבי's warning, to רבי שמואל's limits, to safe distances, to רבי מאיר's exaggeration, and ends with רב's animal calls.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The call for an ox — 'hen hen.'
The call for a lion — 'zeh zeh.'
The call for a camel — 'da da.'
The call for a ship —
phrases.notes: The chant of workers hauling a boat with ropes.

phrases.english: 'heleni, hayya, hela, vehilook, hulya.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves by association from oxen to the calls used for various animals
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each animal, and a ship, has its own traditional driving call.

steps.title: אביי lists six things that cause צרעת
steps.stepSummary: אביי lists six things that cause 'דבר אחר', a polite name for צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Hide, fish, a cup, hot water, eggs, and white lice all cause 'the other thing' (צרעת).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a short, coded list of six things that can cause צרעת. The next step will explain what each word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is short code words that are easy to memorize. Each word stands for a specific habit. On its own the list is unclear, so the גמרא decodes it right after.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The other thing', a polite name for צרעת (leprosy)

steps.confusionAlert: 'דבר אחר' does not mean 'something else' here. It is a polite way of saying צרעת, so the disease is not named directly.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Hide, fish, and a cup,
hot water, and eggs, and white lice —
all of them cause the 'other thing' (leprosy).
phrases.notes: A polite way of not naming the disease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of practical health and safety warnings from steps 10-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six habits (hide, fish, cup, hot water, eggs, white lice) cause צרעת.

steps.title: Explaining each item on the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decodes each of אביי's six code words into a specific harmful habit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hide means sleeping on an untanned tanner's hide. Fish means the שיבוטא fish in the days of ניסן. Cup means leftovers of small fried fish. Hot water means pouring very hot water on yourself. Eggs means stepping on eggshells. White lice means washing a garment and wearing it again before eight days pass, which creates lice. All of these cause צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through אביי's list one by one and explains what habit each word refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one-word code turns into a real case. For example, 'fish' does not mean all fish, only the שיבוטא in ניסן. The last item also explains how the harm happens: re-wearing a washed garment too soon breeds lice.

phrases.english: Hide — one who sleeps on a tanner's hide.
Fish — the shibuta fish in the days of Nisan.
Cup — the leftovers of a dish of small fried fish.
Hot water — very hot water that one pours on himself.
Eggs — one who steps on eggshells.
White lice — one who washes his garment
and does not keep it aside for eight days
and then wears it again —
these lice are created,
and they cause the 'other thing' (leprosy).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each code word in אביי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each code word stands for a specific habit that causes צרעת.

steps.title: Don't walk barefoot in a house with a cat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא warns not to enter a house with a cat barefoot, because the cat may have left sharp snake bones on the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In a house with a cat, a person should not walk in without shoes. Why? Because the cat kills snakes and eats them, and snakes have tiny bones. If a snake bone gets stuck in a person's foot, it cannot be removed, and he is in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a safety warning and explains the reason himself, using a 'מאי טעמא' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cat is good because it kills snakes. But it leaves behind tiny bones that are dangerous to bare feet, so the danger comes from the cat's own good work. The answer to 'מאי טעמא' lays out each link in that chain.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A house in which there is a cat —

phrases.aramaic: לָא נֵיעוּל בַּהּ אִינִישׁ בְּלָא מְסָנֵי.
phrases.english: a person should not enter it without shoes.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּשׁוּנָּרָא קָטֵיל לְחִיוְיָא וְאָכֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Because the cat kills a snake and eats it,
and the snake has tiny bones,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי יָתֵיב לֵהּ גַּרְמָא דְחִיוְיָא אַכַּרְעֵיהּ —
phrases.english: and if a snake bone gets stuck in his foot —
it does not come out, and he is in danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בֵּיתָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ שׁוּנָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new safety warning, continuing the theme of dangers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not walk barefoot in a house with a cat, because of snake bones.

steps.title: Another version: don't walk in the dark in a house without a cat
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב פפא's warning was the opposite case: in a house with no cat, don't walk in the dark, because a snake may be there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: In a house with no cat, a person should not walk in the dark. Why? Because a snake might wrap itself around him without his knowing, and he will be in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב פפא's warning. This time it is about a house with no cat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the cat is the protection, not the problem. Without a cat, snakes are not hunted and may be in the house, so walking in the dark is dangerous. The two versions do not really clash: one warns about the cat's leftovers, the other about having no cat at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the statement)

phrases.english: Some say:
A house in which there is no cat —
a person should not enter it in the dark.
What is the reason?
Perhaps a snake will wrap itself around him
and he will not know, and he will be in danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: בֵּיתָא דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ שׁוּנָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב פפא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not walk in the dark in a house with no cat, because snakes may be there.

steps.title: Three instructions: first, don't make a blemish on yourself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי gave רבי three instructions. A memory aid (מק״ש) is given, and the first is: do not make a blemish on yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי commanded רבי three things (memory sign: מ-ק-ש): Do not make a blemish on yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a list of three pieces of advice and gives the first one. It is worded in a puzzling way, so the next step asks what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The memory sign מק״ש helps remember the three: מ for מום (blemish), ק for מקח (purchase), ש for אשתך (your wife). 'Don't make a blemish on yourself' sounds like it is about the body. The גמרא will show it is advice about protecting yourself.

phrases.english: Three things commanded

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֶת רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei to Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi):
(Mem-Kuf-Shin is the mnemonic)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for the key words: מום, מקח, אשתך.

phrases.english: Do not make a blemish on yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֶת רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list of life advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First instruction: do not make a blemish on yourself.

steps.title: What does 'a blemish on yourself' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the first instruction means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'do not make a blemish on yourself' means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are unclear, since they could be read as literal physical harm. The question asks for the real practical meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What does it mean?)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of 'do not make a blemish on yourself'.

steps.title: Don't take on a court case against three people
steps.stepSummary: The meaning: don't have a lawsuit against three people, because one will be the opponent and two can be witnesses against you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not have a court case against three people, because one will be your opponent and the other two will be witnesses against you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the 'blemish' is the damage you bring on yourself by fighting three people in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are enough to decide a case. If three people are against you, one can sue while the other two testify for him, and you will lose. Getting into that fight is a 'blemish' you caused yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: The other side in a court case

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֶּיהְוֵי לָךְ דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵי תְּלָתָא,
phrases.english: Do not have a court case against three people,
because one will be your opponent
and two will be witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֶּיהְוֵי לָךְ דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵי תְּלָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'blemish' is a court case against three people, where two can testify for the third against you.

steps.title: Second instruction: don't act like a buyer without money
steps.stepSummary: Do not stand over an item as if you will buy it when you have no money to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not stand over a purchase at a time when you have no money.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second of the three instructions (the ק in מק״ש). Don't act interested in buying something you cannot pay for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pretending to be a buyer misleads the seller and gets his hopes up for nothing. It is a form of dishonesty, so a person should only bargain when he really can buy.

phrases.english: And do not stand over a purchase
at a time when you have no money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the list of three instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not act like a buyer when you cannot pay.

steps.title: Third instruction: wait after your wife immerses
steps.stepSummary: After your wife immerses, do not be intimate with her on the first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If your wife immersed, do not be intimate with her on the first night.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third instruction (the ש in מק״ש, for אשתך). It is an extra stringency to wait one night after טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once a wife has immersed she is permitted right away. This advice adds a stricter waiting period. The next step tells us which case it means and why.

phrases.english: Your wife immersed —
do not be intimate with her on the first night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list of three instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not be intimate on the first night after your wife's immersion.

steps.title: רב limits the rule to a Torah-level נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the third instruction applies to a נדה by Torah law. Since her flow was open, she might continue to see blood and become a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This is about a נדה by Torah law. Since her flow is known to be open, perhaps her זיבה bleeding will continue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב narrows the third instruction to one case and explains the worry behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a נדה who bled may immerse right after seven days, even if she bled all seven days. Since her flow was just active, it might start again, and then she would be a זבה. Waiting one more night protects against that.

keyTerms.meaning: A נדה by Torah law (before the later stringency of seven clean days)
זבה bleeding, a more serious status

steps.whatToRemember: The three instructions of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי (מק״ש): no court case against three people, no acting like a buyer without money, and wait a night after immersion. רב applies the last one to a Torah-level נדה whose flow might continue.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows an early worry about blood flow coming back right after immersion. This connects to the later practice of being extra careful with נדה and זבה.

phrases.english: Rav said:
And this is about a niddah by Torah law,
since the flow is presumed to be open,
perhaps zava bleeding will continue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the third instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiting night applies to a Torah-level נדה, because her open flow might continue as זיבה.

steps.title: Three warnings to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה warned רבי about three dangers: going out alone at night, standing undressed before a candle, and entering a new bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי the son of רבי יהודה commanded רבי about three things: Do not go out alone at night. Do not stand undressed in front of a candle. Do not enter a new bathhouse, because it might collapse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new list of three warnings. The next steps explain each warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the bathhouse warning comes with a reason here: the new building might collapse. The other two warnings get their reasons later, each from a ברייתא. The order of explanation in the coming steps does not follow the order of the list.

keyTerms.meaning: it will collapse or cave in

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. It does not mean 'some rabbi'.

phrases.english: Three things commanded

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶת רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda to Rebbi:
Do not go out alone at night,
and do not stand undressed before a candle,
and do not enter a new bathhouse,
lest it collapse.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צִוָּה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶת רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of three warnings, matching the earlier lists of instructions on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not go out alone at night, do not stand undressed before a candle, and do not enter a new bathhouse.

steps.title: How long is a bathhouse new?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a bathhouse counts as 'new'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the third warning. It wants to know how long the danger of a 'new' bathhouse lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning used the word 'new' without giving a time limit. The גמרא wants a clear measure so a person knows when the bathhouse becomes safe.

keyTerms.meaning: until how long? (asking for a limit)

phrases.english: Until how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit of the 'new bathhouse' warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long a bathhouse counts as new.

steps.title: Twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that a bathhouse counts as new for twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Until twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A bathhouse is 'new' for its first twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a full year of use, the building has proven it is stable, so the fear of collapse goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: an early אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Until twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bathhouse is considered new for twelve months.

steps.title: Why not stand undressed before a candle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the candle warning with a ברייתא: standing undressed before a candle makes a person נכפה, and intimacy by candlelight leads to children who are נכפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And do not stand undressed before a candle' is as it was taught in a ברייתא: One who stands undressed before a candle becomes epileptic. And one who is intimate by candlelight will have epileptic children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second warning and gives its source and reason from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning in step 25 gave no reason. The ברייתא shows the danger is to health: it can cause epilepsy. It also adds a related case about intimacy by candlelight, which affects the children.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
one who is intimate with his wife
by the light of a candle

phrases.english: 'And do not stand undressed before a candle,'
as it was taught: One who stands undressed before a candle —
becomes epileptic.
And one who is intimate by candlelight —
will have epileptic children.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל תַּעֲמוֹד בִּפְנֵי הַנֵּר עָרוֹם, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bathhouse topic and returns to explain the second warning.
steps.raayaObject: The warning not to stand undressed before a candle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying this causes epilepsy.

steps.title: A baby sleeping in the bed
steps.stepSummary: A related ברייתא: if a man is intimate on a bed where a baby is sleeping, that baby becomes נכפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who is intimate on a bed where a baby is sleeping, that baby becomes epileptic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא on the same theme of things that cause epilepsy. The next three steps limit this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This expands the topic from the candle case. Here the harm falls on a third person, the baby sleeping on the bed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who is intimate on a bed
on which a baby is sleeping —
that baby becomes epileptic.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ עַל מִטָּה שֶׁתִּינוֹק יָשֵׁן עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case of something that causes epilepsy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intimacy on a bed where a baby sleeps makes the baby epileptic.

steps.title: First limit: only under one year old
steps.stepSummary: The danger applies only if the baby is under one year old.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when the baby is not yet one year old. But if he is one year old, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first of three limits on the baby rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby under a year is more fragile. Once the child is a year old, the concern no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when (introduces a limit)
we have no problem with it

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he is not one year old,
but if he is one year old —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָוֵי בַּר שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the baby rule by the baby's age.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger applies only to a baby under one year.

steps.title: Second limit: only near the feet
steps.stepSummary: The danger applies only if the baby sleeps near the father's feet, not near his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when the baby sleeps by his feet. But if the baby sleeps by his head, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second limit, which depends on where the baby is lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Near the feet, the baby is close to the place of intimacy. Near the head, the baby is far enough away that there is no danger.

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he sleeps by his feet,
but if he sleeps by his head —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּגָנֵי לַהֲדֵי כַּרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit, based on where the baby lies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger applies only if the baby sleeps near the feet.

steps.title: Third limit: no hand placed on the baby
steps.stepSummary: The danger applies only if the father does not place his hand on the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he does not put his hand on the baby. But if he puts his hand on the baby, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third and last limit on the baby rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a hand on the baby acts as a barrier between the baby and the act. That removes the danger.
steps.whatToRemember: The baby rule has three limits. The danger exists only when (1) the baby is under a year old, (2) the baby sleeps by the feet, and (3) no hand is placed on the baby.

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he does not place his hand on him,
but if he places his hand on him —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מַנַּח יְדֵיהּ עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final limit to the baby rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing a hand on the baby removes the danger.

steps.title: Why not go out alone at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the first warning: on Tuesday nights and Friday nights, אגרת בת מחלת goes out with 180,000 מלאכי חבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not go out alone at night' is as it was taught in a ברייתא: A person should not go out alone at night, not on Tuesday nights and not on Friday nights, because אגרת בת מחלת goes out with 180,000 destructive angels, and each one of them has permission to harm on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the first warning, going out alone at night, and gives its reason from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא narrows the danger to two specific nights and names the source of danger: אגרת בת מחלת and her huge group of harmful forces. Each one can do harm by itself, so the danger is very great.

keyTerms.meaning: Tuesday nights (the night going into Wednesday)
Friday nights (the night going into שבת)
the name of a chief of the שדים (demons)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לילי רביעיות' is Tuesday night, the night before Wednesday, because the Jewish day starts at night. In the same way, 'לילי שבתות' is Friday night.

phrases.english: 'Do not go out alone at night,' as it was taught:
One should not go out alone at night,
not on Tuesday nights
and not on Friday nights,
because Agrat daughter of Machalat,
she and 180,000
destructive angels go out,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת
phrases.english: and each and every one has permission
to harm on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to explain the first warning from step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The warning not to go out alone at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about אגרת בת מחלת going out on Tuesday nights and Friday nights.

steps.title: At first they were out every day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: at first, these harmful forces were present every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Originally they were found every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a story that will explain why the danger is limited to only two nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line tells us the limit to two nights was not always the case. The story that follows explains how the change came about.

phrases.english: Originally they were found every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story explaining the two-night limit in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At first, the harmful forces were out every day.

steps.title: אגרת threatens רבי חנינא בן דוסא
steps.stepSummary: אגרת met רבי חנינא בן דוסא and told him she would have harmed him, if Heaven had not announced to be careful with him and his Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once she met רבי חנינא בן דוסא. She said to him: If they had not announced about you in Heaven, 'Be careful with חנינא and his תורה,' I would have put you in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אגרת admits she cannot harm רבי חנינא בן דוסא because Heaven protects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heaven's announcement shows how great רבי חנינא בן דוסא was. This sets up his next move: he uses that standing against her.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא famous for his holiness and miracles

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנָא חֲדָא פְּגַעָה בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא,
phrases.english: Once she met Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
she said to him:
If they did not announce about you in Heaven:
'Be careful with Chanina and his Torah' — I would have endangered you.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִמְנָא חֲדָא פְּגַעָה בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with the meeting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven protected רבי חנינא בן דוסא from אגרת.

steps.title: He bans her from settled places
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא decrees that she may never pass through inhabited places.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: If I am important in Heaven, I decree on you that you never pass through a settled place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בן דוסא turns her own words against her and uses his standing in Heaven to ban her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She admitted he is important in Heaven, so he uses that importance to issue a decree. The decree would protect people completely, since she could never enter where people live.

phrases.english: He said to her:
If I am important in Heaven,
I decree upon you
that you never pass through settled places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חנינא בן דוסא responds to her threat with a decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא banned אגרת from settled places.

steps.title: She is left two nights
steps.stepSummary: אגרת begs for a little room, and he leaves her Friday nights and Tuesday nights. This explains the ברייתא's two nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Please, I beg you, leave me a little space. He left her Friday nights and Tuesday nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. This explains why the ברייתא warns only about Tuesday nights and Friday nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ban was eased to allow her two nights. That is why the danger of going out alone, once present every day, is now limited to those nights.
steps.whatToRemember: The warning not to go out alone at night applies especially on Tuesday nights and Friday nights. Those are the only nights רבי חנינא בן דוסא left to אגרת בת מחלת.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story connects back to the ברייתא in step 33 and gives the reason for its two-night limit.

phrases.english: She said to him:
I beg of you,
leave me a little space.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבַק לַהּ לֵילֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת וְלֵילֵי רְבִיעִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: He left her Friday nights and Tuesday nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story and explains the two nights in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The harmful forces are now out only on Tuesday nights and Friday nights, so those are the nights of danger.

steps.title: אגרת meets אביי and admits Heaven protects him
steps.stepSummary: A second story: אגרת met אביי and told him she would have harmed him, except that Heaven announced to be careful with נחמני and his Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: once she met אביי and said to him, 'If they did not announce about you in Heaven, "Be careful with נחמני and his Torah," I would have put you in danger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second story about אגרת, this time with אביי. It sets up a second decree that mirrors the one made by רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story copies the earlier one almost word for word. The only change is the name: the earlier story was about רבי חנינא בן דוסא, and this one is about נחמני (אביי). This shows that אביי's Torah also gave him Heavenly protection.

keyTerms.meaning: She met him; she came upon him
I would have put you in danger

steps.confusionAlert: נחמני is not a new person. It is אביי himself. He was raised by רבה בר נחמני, and some say נחמני was his real name.

phrases.english: And furthermore: one time
she (Agrat) met Abaye,
she said to him:
If not that they announce about you in Heaven:
phrases.notes: The same Heavenly announcement as in the earlier story

phrases.english: "Be careful with Nachmani and his Torah"
— I would have endangered you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: חֲדָא זִמְנָא פְּגַעָה בֵּיהּ בְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second parallel story to the רבי חנינא בן דוסא story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven protected אביי because of his Torah, just as it protected רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

steps.title: אביי decrees that she may never pass through inhabited places
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that if he is important in Heaven, he decrees that she may never pass through inhabited places.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: 'If I am important in Heaven, I decree on you that you may never pass through inhabited places.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses his importance in Heaven to make a decree banning אגרת from places where people live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי turns her own words against her: if Heaven values me, then my decree has force. This matches רבי חנינא בן דוסא's decree, and it sets up the question that comes next.

phrases.english: He said to her:
If I am important in Heaven,
I decree upon you
that you never pass through inhabited places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי responds to אגרת's statement with a decree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי banned אגרת from inhabited places forever.

steps.title: But we see that they do pass through
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the stories: we can see that harmful forces still pass through inhabited places.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that she does pass through!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a strong question. If these decrees were made, why do we still see harmful forces in places where people live?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great people decreed that אגרת may never pass through inhabited places. Yet experience shows that harmful forces are still around. The challenge compares the decrees against reality.

keyTerms.meaning: But we see (a challenge from what we can observe)

phrases.english: But we see
that she passes through?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the decrees from both stories
steps.kashyaTarget: The decrees of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and אביי banning harmful forces from inhabited places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What we observe (harmful forces still pass through inhabited places) seems to contradict the decrees.

steps.title: The answer begins: these ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: 'These ones...' The rest continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: These...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the question. The full answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הָנֵי ('these') signals that the answer will point to some specific case that explains why the decree does not cover what we see. Only the opening word of the answer appears on this amud, and its content comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) say; introduces an answer

phrases.english: They say: These
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 40
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (begun here); its content continues on the next amud
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decrees should have removed all harmful forces from inhabited places.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer continues on the next amud.
